chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: A man swore by disavowal from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then broke his oath. What is his repentance, and what is his expiation?
So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: “He feeds ten needy persons, for each needy person one mudd, and he seeks forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.الْبَرَاءَةِ: disavowal or dissociation invoked in an oath
key_terms.مَسَاكِينَ: needy persons entitled to be fed
key_terms.مُدٌّ: a measured quantity of food given to each needy person

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for swearing disassociation from Allah or the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and then breaking the oath?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who swears an oath of disassociation from Allah or from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and then breaks it. The expiation is to feed ten needy persons, giving each one mudd, along with seeking Allah’s forgiveness as repentance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4330 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, wrote to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (as) asking about a man who swore an oath of disassociation from Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, or from the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) and then broke his oath. What is his repentance and expiation?
Imam (as) responded: "He should feed ten needy people, giving each needy person one mudd of food, and seek forgiveness from Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious."
